content: 1. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. Follow local regulations or consult your pharmacist for proper disposal methods. 2. This information was last revised in May 2024. 3. This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. 4. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 5. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically four times a day (every six hours). To minimize stomach upset, do not swallow all capsules for one dose at the same time. 6. This medication works best when the drug level in your body is maintained at a constant level. Take it at evenly spaced intervals. 7. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. 8. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Refer to the How to Use section for tips on reducing stomach upset. 9. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. 10. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. 11. Before taking flucytosine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. 12. Flucytosine may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections (e.g., chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, flu). 13. Inform your healthcare professional that you are using flucytosine before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. 14. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not recommended during the first three months of pregnancy as it may harm an unborn baby. 15. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. 16. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. 17. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 18. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., serum creatinine), potentially causing false test results. 19. In case of overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 20. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney/liver function, blood cell counts, blood mineral levels) should be performed regularly. Keep all medical and lab appointments. 21. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. 22. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. 23. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 24. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
